_comment: Which rail each capacitor sits on, and what that rail runs at.
The rated voltage is NOT here -- it is read from the parts list at run time,
so a corrected BOM corrects this too.
source: 'schematic' means the net was traced on the Chapter 7 sheet named in
the note, at full resolution. All eleven entries here were traced on sheet 1
of 3; none is inferred, and none has appliedV left null.
A6 has ELEVEN electrolytics and they are all tantalum: C1-C8 and C49-C51, one
part number for all of them (CAP,TA,4.7UF,+-20%,25V, stock 807644). There is
no aluminium can anywhere on this assembly -- every other capacitor in Table
6-7 is ceramic or polyester, so this is the whole recap list. All eleven sit
in the supply entry and rail-generation circuit in the bottom left of sheet 1,
which makes the audit unusually tidy: one part type, one circuit, one sheet.
Rail voltages come from A17's dataset, which reads them off Table 2-10 and the
Figure 7-21 sheet 1 annotations -- +17 S is 17.475 V and -17 S is -17.865 V,
not a round 17 -- because A6 makes none of the four rails that arrive on P101.
The local rails are computed from those and from the zener values printed on
sheet 1, and each note says which. Magnitudes are entered unsigned.
The worst margin on the board is 70% of rating (C7 and C8 on +17 S). Nothing
comes close to its limit and nothing exceeds it -- a ratio over 1.0 would have
meant the rating or the rail was recorded wrong, not that Fluke had shipped a
part that fails on power-up.
railClass is how much energy is behind the rail, which decides what a shorted
part does. These letters are this board's:
A  +17 S and -17 S from A17's regulators, referenced to S COM. Regulated,
and NOT fused anywhere on this assembly -- there is no F designator in
Table 6-7 at all, so A17's protection upstream of P101 is the only limit.
B  +5 LH and -5 LH logic supplies from A17, referenced to LH COM (C1, C3) or
to SCOM (C2, C4) depending on which side of the entry choke they sit.
Regulated, and unfused on this board for the same reason.
C  -5F, made on THIS board by choke L12 from -5 LH. Same energy as class B,
one filter section further along.
D  the shunt-regulated local rails +12 and -9.5, made on this board by a
zener and a dropper. Energy-limited by R39 (12K) and R40 (10K), so these
two are the only capacitors here behind any current limit at all.

C7.note: Sheet 1 of 3: the +17 S bypass on the source side of entry choke L4, straight across P101 pins 22A/22C to S COM. 70% of a 25 V part and the worst margin on this board, which is not alarming for a solid tantalum on a regulated rail but is the pair to replace first if any recapping is done. Its partner on the load side of L4 is C8.

C8.note: Sheet 1 of 3: the +17 S bypass on the LOAD side of choke L4, to SCOM, and the node the whole +17 S distribution and VR1's +12 dropper hang off. Same 70% of rating as C7. Note that this is the rail §5-5 step 13 calls the '~+17V' high level at U13's collectors, so a soft C8 shows up as ringing on that measurement rather than as a supply fault.

C5.note: Sheet 1 of 3: the -17 S bypass on the source side of entry choke L3, across P101 pins 23A/23C to S COM. 71% of a 25 V part -- fractionally the tightest of the eleven, because -17 S runs slightly further from zero than +17 S does. The mirror of C7.

C6.note: Sheet 1 of 3: the -17 S bypass on the LOAD side of choke L3, to SCOM, and the node that feeds both zener chains -- VR4 to -12 and VR5/CR8/CR9 to -11 and -9.5. The mirror of C8, and the same 71% of rating.

C1.note: Sheet 1 of 3: across the incoming -5 LH rail at P101 pins 20A/20C, and returned to LH COM (18A/18C) rather than to SCOM -- it is on the source side of entry choke L1, in the LH COM domain. 20% of a 25 V part. The two commons matter here: C2, one choke further along, returns to SCOM instead.

C2.note: Sheet 1 of 3: the -5 LH bypass on the LOAD side of choke L1, to SCOM. This is the -5LH net that feeds the ECL parts before L12 makes -5F from it. 20% of rating.

C3.note: Sheet 1 of 3: across the incoming +5 LH rail at P101 pins 16A/16C to LH COM, the mirror of C1 and on the same side of the entry chokes. 20% of a 25 V part.

C4.note: Sheet 1 of 3: the +5 LH bypass on the LOAD side of choke L2, to SCOM. The node R66 and R67 divide to make the +2.5 V reference for the comparators in U7, U10 and U11, so a failure here moves every filter-select and multiplexer threshold at once. 20% of rating.

C49.note: Sheet 1 of 3: the reservoir for -5F, the rail choke L12 and this capacitor make from -5LH (§2-217 names both parts). -5F is the quiet negative supply for the ECL sections; it is the same 5 V as its parent, so 20% of a 25 V part. This is the only one of the eleven that is not on a rail arriving at P101 or a zener node.

C50.note: Sheet 1 of 3, and the one that would be recorded wrongly by reading the feed rail instead of the node. C50 is NOT on +17 S: VR1, a 5.1 V zener, sits between +17S and this node with R39 (12K) as its load, so the node is +17.475 - 5.1 = 12.4 V and the capacitor sees 12.4 V, not 17.5. 50% of a 25 V part. The 12.4 V is computed from A17's +17 S nominal and VR1's marked voltage; the sheet's own net label is simply '+12'.

C51.note: Sheet 1 of 3, and the second node that must be traced rather than assumed. C51 is NOT on -17 S: VR5 (6.2 V) drops from -17S to the -11 node, then CR8 and CR9 (1N4448) come back up two diode drops to the node C51 and R40 (10K) are on, which the sheet labels -9.5. Tracing it gives -17.865 + 6.2 = -11.665 at the VR5 knee and about -10.4 after two 0.6 V drops, which is what is entered; the printed label says -9.5, and the worst case if either diode opens is the -11.7 V at the knee. Every one of those numbers is under half the 25 V rating, so the choice between them changes nothing about the margin -- but the number to have written down is the traced one, not the rail feeding the chain.
